mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand and economic expansion, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of periods with sustained HOUST increases, or the correlation between HOUST growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending power increases.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals increased economic activity and supply, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period, it indicates strong consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > CPIAUCSL growth over 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of periods with RSAFS outpacing CPIAUCSL, or the interaction effect between RSAFS and CPIAUCSL growth rates on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of decreasing unemployment (UNRATE) and increasing nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over a 3-month period signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases over 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect between UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% for more than 6 months signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as liquidity flows into equities.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of periods with FEDFUNDS below 1%, or the correlation between sustained low FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals a contraction in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
